name: Shakti remote-viewing design (untested): modulated 40 Hz occipital
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software; extrapolation from Persinger-lab papers)
summary: Murphy's proposed Shakti design for remote viewing: the modulated 40 Hz signal over both occipital lobes. The 20 min are this project's choice; Murphy gives no duration. He links the design to the occipital 7 Hz activity Persinger's lab reported in the remote viewer Ingo Swann, and writes that it 'has not been tested in practice'.
setting: Practise remote-viewing exercises (Murphy). For a fair test, judge results blind, e.g. with the app's Photo-target trial guide.
schedule: The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: The vendor proposes its modulated 40 Hz signal over the occipital lobes and says it 'has not been tested in practice for enhancement of remote viewing skills' (remote_v.htm, REMOTE VIEWING). No duration is given. The occipital lobes lie 'above the bony ridge at the back of the head' (bi_occipital.htm). This program plays 20 min on four coils over the occipital lobes (O1, PO3, O2, PO4), all with the same signal; the other four stay unused. The 20 min and the sites are this project's choices. The vendor's file is not published and no parameters are given. It is rebuilt as a continuous 40 Hz sine whose phase swings 3 rad ahead of and behind a steady 40 Hz every 2 s (about 38.5 to 41.5 Hz), in 1-ms points; the modulation is this project's choice. The two-phase design (frontal, then occipital) is murphy-shakti-psi-rv-untested. Field strength: the vendor calibrates this signal at 10 mG (1 uT) 'when measured from one coil' (obe45_consent.htm). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. The default 1 uT there is about 56 uT at the coil face, well above the vendor's calibration. Support: none for this design. In the study Murphy draws on, one subject (Ingo Swann) was exposed to a field in a single 30-min sitting and sketched distant targets several times on the days after; his occipital 7 Hz activity per trial correlated moderately with accuracy (rho = .50) (Persinger 2002 p.1 [927]). One subject, one lab, not independently repeated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The vendor says blurry vision is possible in principle, though not reported (bi_occipital.htm): stop if your sight changes. Do not use results for decisions about real people, places or money. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
source: Murphy, Shakti demo: Remote viewing https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/remote_v.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Psychic skills https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/psychic.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Modulated 40 Hz (obe45) signal (10 mG calibration) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/obe45_consent.htm ; Persinger et al. 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927 (remote viewing with Ingo Swann) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Safety - how often https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/how_often_is_safe.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Taking breaks https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/break.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 (8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal, sham-controlled) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
